text:
Maya (infra): Heads up: seeing a big spike of pod disconnects in gpupool-east1a around 10:12 UTC. ~120 restarts in 5m. node-762 shows 'nf_conntrack: table full' in kernel logs.

infra-bot: Deployment 'model-train' rolled out to gpupool-east1a at 09:58 UTC (canary 20%).

Ravi: On it. Can you paste dmesg from node-762 and conntrack stats?

Maya (infra): dmesg | tail -n50 showed: 
```
[ 12345.678901] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
[ 12345.679012] nf_conntrack: dropping conntrack entry for src=10.32.5.12:59234 dst=10.32.9.3:80
```
and conntrack -S snapshot: 
```
cpu=0 flow_entries=65536

tcp    51234
udp    234
icmp   0
```

Joel: Looks like conntrack entries are sky high and ephemeral ports are getting exhausted on SNAT. What's net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max?

Maya (infra): sysctl shows net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 65536 (default-ish). net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 32768 61000.

Ravi: We have a lot of short-lived outbound connections from sidecars + the model prefetcher. If east-west traffic is being SNATed by our nodes (hairpin), each east-west handshake creates additional tuples. Also RDMA fallback paths can create odd tuple churn.

Izzy: Are we seeing NAT hairpinning? East-west within same VPC but SNAT applied by our egress/masquerade rules would multiply tuples per connection.

Maya (infra): Yes — we still have the MASQUERADE rule active on the nodes for pod egress to certain services (added last month to handle legacy egress-proxy).

Joel: Immediate mitigation: bump nf_conntrack_max to 262144 and tune hashsize. Example: 
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120
```

Maya (infra): I pushed that to node-762 via salt: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144. After the change entries dropped to ~60k and kernel messages stopped. Pods stopped restarting.

sre-oncall: This is a bandaid. Root cause track: 1) remove unnecessary SNAT for intra-cluster pod CIDR, 2) adjust iptables/kube-proxy so pod->pod east-west doesn't hit MASQUERADE, 3) adjust app to reuse connections instead of short lived churn.

Ravi: Agreed. Also we should add conntrack usage as a metric with alerts at 60% and 80% so we get earlier visibility. I'll open an infra ticket and a Datadog dashboard tile.

infra-bot: Ticket INFRA-1128 created: "conntrack spike gpupool-east1a: audit SNAT rules + exporter"

Maya (infra): Note: rolling kernel bump to 5.10.102 on this pool last week reduced hash collisions but didn't eliminate the blowups — the real multiplier is the SNAT + aggressive prefetch behavior from the model training sidecars.

Joel: Action items: Ravi -> ticket + alert; Maya -> emergency playbook (how to increase nf_conntrack_max and drain safely); Izzy -> audit iptables rules and test bypass for pod CIDR on lab node. Consider long-term: move to eBPF SNAT (Cilium) or reconfigure iptables to avoid node-level MASQUERADE for intra-pod traffic.

Izzy: I'll run a lab test to add an iptables rule to bypass MASQUERADE for pod CIDR and stress with the prefetcher. If stable, we'll template and rollout with daemonset.

sre-oncall: :thumbsup: Follow-up: schedule a 2hr maintenance window tonight to roll the fix if testing passes. Also include a postmortem if INFRA-1128 shows missing alerts.

Ravi: Created the Datadog conntrack dashboard and set alerts. I'll link the dashboard in the ticket.

Maya (infra): Temporary note in runbook: when conntrack table full and pods restarting -> 1) increase nf_conntrack_max 2) drain and cordon worst nodes 3) validate ipv4 ip_local_port_range 4) check for unintended MASQUERADE rules.

Joel: Also check kube-proxy conntrack settings and conntrack-max at kube-proxy if running iptables mode. Long-term, prefer connection pooling in the prefetcher and reduce per-request ephemeral ports.

Izzy: I'll report back with lab results by EOD.

Maya (infra): Thanks team — saving this thread into INFRA-1128 so we can include logs + commands used.
